requirements.description: Implement the core functionality before creating the reference examples and language ports.
Provide the static `EnviormentsOptions` entry point for validated startup configuration and application/runtime identity.
Automatically attach application name, build version, deployment environment, instance, host, OS, and available runtime context to events.
Configure human, coding-agent, and log-collector output through documented environment variables.
Keep all shipping core code free of third-party NuGet dependencies, including transitive runtime dependencies. Prefer zero explicit package references in the core itself.
Preserve published backwards compatibility indefinitely, including source, binary, configuration, wire format, and documented behavior.
Execute and distribute the complete unit, integration, mutation, architecture, backwards-compatibility, and business-case verification material with every published version.
Demonstrate readable C# and enforce responsibility and dependency boundaries automatically.
Keep the core usable across applications without a dependency on CIS orchestration, CTEP persistence, a game engine, or a collector SDK.
Preserve a language-neutral contract and fixtures that a later TypeScript implementation can pass.

stories.title: Establish package identities and supported framework contracts
stories.user_story: As a library maintainer, I want identities and supported targets fixed before publication so consumers can depend on a stable upgrade contract.
stories.outcome: The repository has one explicit identity and target policy before any public baseline exists.

tasks.description: Inspect the first intended consumer's project target without migrating or changing that application; record whether net10.0 satisfies it and add any necessary older target before publication.
Choose final package IDs, assembly names, namespaces, and bridge identity using the repository convention; retain the exact EnviormentsOptions type name.
Record the guide's assembly-version/signing choice and assess intended loader scenarios; distinguish assembly identity from advancing package, file, and informational versions.
Create separate contract-target and actual execution-matrix records for Windows and Linux, with explicit historical-runtime and roll-forward treatment.

acceptance_criteria.description: The identity record names both shipping packages, their namespaces, signing policy, and all initial target assets without relying on Core shorthand.
The inspected consumer target and its source location are recorded; any additional target is in the initial contract before publication.
Execution claims cover only recorded Windows/Linux lanes; optional platforms or modes have no unsupported success claim.
The target-retention policy prohibits dropping published assets, raising their minimum framework, or rewriting old consumers to satisfy an upgrade.

stories.business_case_role: enables future compatibility evidence

stories.title: Create the minimal repository and enforce shipping dependency boundaries
stories.user_story: As a core consumer, I want shipping dependencies and responsibility boundaries enforced so the library remains independent of application infrastructure.
stories.outcome: A minimal core package demonstrates the dependency and maintainability constraints mechanically.

tasks.description: Create the Core, optional Core.MicrosoftLogging, five functional test-family projects, TestSupport, contracts, compatibility, verification/mutation, examples, and eng structure from section 5.

Apply nullable/compiler warnings as errors, SDK analyzers, documentation output, deterministic Release builds, formatting rules, and the documented decomposition review triggers.
Pack the minimal core and inspect its dependency groups/assets and assembly references; add a deliberately forbidden dependency fixture that the initial gate must reject.

acceptance_criteria.description: The minimal core has zero explicit PackageReference items, no larger convenience framework reference, and no third-party runtime assets.
The bridge and test/tool dependencies are isolated and have an explicit allowlist; neither can flow back into the core.
Release build, documentation/analyzer checks, and dotnet format --verify-no-changes succeed for the legitimate scaffold.
The forbidden-dependency fixture makes verification fail with the violated rule identified; no broad suppression is used.

stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want the pinned toolchain proved against real core behavior early so full verification is feasible and reproducible.
stories.outcome: The chosen SDK, test runner, coverage collector, compatibility tool, and mutation engine work together on a real core behavior.

Commit global.json, central versions, project lockfiles, local tool manifest, NuGet restore configuration/source mapping, and approved dependency inventory.

The known branching behavior produces a nonzero branch denominator with Microsoft's collector/tool rather than an accidentally selected Coverlet collector.

stories.business_case_role: verification enabler

stories.title: Bootstrap verification commands, test inventories, and deterministic support
stories.user_story: As a reviewer, I want one driver to expose discovery and missing work so incomplete scaffolding cannot appear release-ready.

tasks.description: Create repository-owned entry points for eng/verify developer and release profiles, eng/replay, and eng/check-release with structured output, documented prerequisites, explicit stage exits, and stable report paths.

Every family has an independently identifiable discovery/execution/report slot, including mutation without inventing a sixth C# test project.

stories.title: Define immutable startup, identity, and configuration contracts
stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want a stable startup and configuration contract so applications initialize the core consistently.
stories.outcome: The environment API and every configuration interpretation have a reviewable contract before resolver implementation.

tasks.description: Define EnvironmentSetup, immutable EnvironmentSnapshot/resolved logging/EventMetadata, EnvironmentKind values, configuration issue types, and EnviormentsOptions signatures/convenience getters.
Record pre-initialization, failed validation, single successful publication, concurrent initialization, repeated initialization, and no-production-Reset semantics.
Encode all section 8 keys, aliases, defaults, units, accepted tokens/bounds, precedence, blank handling, invalid higher-priority behavior, and one-time path resolution in machine-readable fixtures.
Define metadata field types, discovery fallbacks, application-assembly identity, BuildVersion versus ServiceVersion, safe diagnostics, and immutable/copying ownership rules.

acceptance_criteria.description: The public contract retains the requested spelling, named setup properties, immutable resolved outputs, and stable enum values. Narrow atomic-publication/synchronization fields are permitted; mutable static option values or operation context are not.
Every documented configuration key has explicit valid, absent/blank, invalid, precedence, and applicable boundary expectations.
Fixtures preserve informational build strings, optional unavailable facts, actual process start versus initialization time, and the distinct telemetry release label.
Initialization and error contracts are documented and compile-time consumer fixtures cover their public shape; implementation completion is not claimed by those contract checks.

stories.business_case_role: contract definition; behavioral execution follows in WP-03

stories.title: Define event schema, supported values, and portable fixtures
stories.user_story: As a structured-log consumer, I want exact event and value contracts so records retain their meaning across applications, upgrades, and later language ports.
stories.outcome: C# implementations and a later TypeScript port have one exact observable event contract.

tasks.description: Define event input/captured-value/scope data contracts and schema v1 with fixed severity, resource projection, timestamps, required/optional fields, and null/absence rules.
Define explicit safe integer, integer-string, decimal-string, finite-number, map/array, UUID, and timestamp representations; specify rejection of arbitrary objects.
Encode every section 9 record, Unicode, node, depth, text, exception, and scope bound, including aggregate encoded-byte accounting and explicit exception truncation.
Create language-neutral valid/rejected fixture pairs for identity projection, correlation/override rules, nested copying, numeric boundaries, escaping, and schema field evolution.

acceptance_criteria.description: Schema fixtures include all required service/env/version and captured resource fields without serializing configuration or destination objects.
Representations are unambiguous across languages: large integers and decimals do not silently switch field types.
Boundary fixtures cover valid Unicode and post-escaping record size, with unsupported/oversized events rejected as specified.
C# contract validation accepts the valid fixture catalog and rejects the invalid catalog; no TypeScript runtime implementation or hosted collector ingestion is marked as tested.

stories.business_case_role: contract fixtures; execution follows in WP-04 and WP-05

stories.outcome: Runtime implementation has fixed signatures and observable result semantics to satisfy.

tasks.description: Specify the complete CoreLogRuntime/CoreLogger method signatures, named arguments, exceptions, diagnostics, scope, provider ownership, and IAsyncDisposable surface.
Define immutable write/flush/stop/output result types, frozen enum values, accepted-only sequence numbers, observed timestamps, rejection snapshots, and global invalid-event accounting.
Encode the argument-validation -> Stopped -> Filtered -> all-faulted rejection -> capture/admission order and the single authoritative severity/deferred-factory rules.

Document per-output ordering, bounded coordination, flush boundaries, cancellation-of-wait, shared stop deadline, loss observations, accounting identity, and accepted/written/flushed/durable distinctions.

acceptance_criteria.description: Contract samples compile without ambiguous nullable overloads, expanding positional options, or multiple authorities for severity.
Decision-table fixtures distinguish all outcomes, including None after closure, partial acceptance, invalid capture, and all-interested-outputs faulted.
Result definitions permit Completed with Succeeded=false and Succeeded=true with LossObserved=true; their meanings and observation boundaries are explicit.
Cancellation and disposal cannot reopen admission or restart the shared shutdown deadline; no API promises disk durability, collector acknowledgement, or cross-output total order.

stories.business_case_role: API and behavioral contract definition

stories.user_story: As an upgrading consumer, I want every published contract retained and represented in immutable history so new releases preserve supported use.
stories.outcome: Future additions preserve every published supported contract, including prereleases.

tasks.description: Review and record the public API, parameter names, constants/enums, construction paths, defaults, target assets, ownership, and behavior for indefinite preservation.

Create the append-only publication/baseline manifest format with package identity membership, version including prerelease, hashes, API metadata, source/binary fixtures, and execution/toolchain records.
Define all four compatibility layers, historical source substitution rules, unchanged binary replay rules, allowed nondeterministic normalization, and zero-history behavior.
Create initial compiling source patterns and deliberately incompatible API/wire samples to qualify the later harness; record which contracts each sample covers.

acceptance_criteria.description: The compatibility policy gives no waiver for a major version, newly added obsolete warning, rewritten baseline, or removed target.
Historical membership comes from the immutable publication record and includes intermediate releases and published prereleases.
The initial manifest accurately represents actual publication history; empty history does not bypass consumer, fixture, or negative-control requirements.
The contract fixture set covers named arguments, null/conversion/extension call patterns, supported implementations, configuration defaults, and wire meanings.

stories.title: Resolve application and runtime identity
stories.outcome: An application receives its own build and process identity through a deterministic resolver, with explicit unavailable values.

tasks.description: Implement identity discovery using supplied application metadata and assembly, with entry-assembly fallback only where available; preserve informational-version strings and explicit commit/build IDs.
Capture process start, host, OS family and description, OS/process architecture, runtime description, and process ID through internal discovery seams.
Keep actual BuildVersion separate from configurable ServiceVersion and generate initialization identity/time through deterministic test seams.
Add table-driven discovery tests and small Windows/Linux process fixtures, including missing optional metadata and application/core assemblies with different versions.

acceptance_criteria.description: Fallback identity identifies the application assembly, never the core assembly; prerelease and build suffixes survive unchanged.
Unavailable optional metadata stays absent; BuildVersion uses its specified unknown fallback, and process start is never replaced with initialization time.
HostName describes the application-visible host; DD_AGENT_HOST does not replace it, and changing a telemetry version override does not change BuildVersion.
Tests prove the expected Windows/Linux projection and macOS family recognition without advertising an untested macOS execution lane.

stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want the core to identify my application and runtime accurately so that each event can be attributed to the binary and instance that produced it.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Resolve documented environment settings and output defaults

Reuse the proven configuration-token behavior from WP01-S03 and resolve every setting in the section 8 table, including independent console/file level inheritance, output enablement, explicit format/stream, queue size, flush interval, shutdown timeout, rotation, and schema selection.
Treat blank values as absent, normalize configuration tokens case-insensitively, and preserve trimmed identity value case; ignore unknown CORE names without dumping process variables.
Add shared input/output configuration fixtures for defaults, aliases, overrides, disabled outputs, and host environment labels; do not mutate the host's resolved framework environment.

acceptance_criteria.description: Fixtures reproduce every documented section 8 default and precedence step, including CORE overrides of DD identity aliases.
A console Warning threshold and file Debug threshold retain the file's Debug interest even when CORE_LOG_LEVEL is Information.
Absent file path or file level None disables file output; console level None disables console output; terminal/debugger state never changes format or stream.
A telemetry environment label can differ from the supplied host framework environment without changing the latter or adding unrelated runtime settings.

stories.user_story: As an operator, I want environment settings to select output behavior consistently so that the same application build can serve human, agent, and collector use cases.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

Validate identity string lengths and control-character rules; collect issues into the immutable CoreConfigurationException issue collection with stable codes and keys.
Capture the initialization working directory and resolve relative CORE_LOG_FILE_PATH values against it once; validate path syntax without creating directories or opening files.
Add boundary and combined-error fixtures, including invalid high-priority input, provided settings for disabled outputs, Unicode, changed working directory, and safe error text.

acceptance_criteria.description: Invalid selected high-priority input fails instead of falling through to a lower-priority value, and recognized supplied output settings are validated even for a disabled output.
Multiple configuration problems appear in one immutable issue collection with stable codes and keys; diagnostics do not expose unrelated variables or credentials.
A relative path is exposed as the expected absolute path, and changing the process working directory after resolution cannot redirect it.
Validation and environment property reads create no directories, open no output, start no worker, and contact no infrastructure.

stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want complete safe startup validation and stable file paths so that configuration errors are understood before output workers start.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

tasks.description: Implement EnviormentsOptions.Initialize, Current, IsInitialized, and the documented convenience getters with a trivial CLR static constructor.
Copy startup input and nested mutable collections into owned immutable resolved options and EventMetadata, then publish only the fully validated snapshot.
Synchronize concurrent initialization so one successful publisher wins, preserve the snapshot after later calls, and allow a failed explicit validation attempt to publish nothing.
Add isolated child-process tests for pre-initialization reads, failed-then-valid initialization, concurrent calls, mutation of setup after initialization, and separate application runs.

acceptance_criteria.description: Current and convenience getters throw the documented InvalidOperationException before successful initialization; failure leaves IsInitialized false.
Concurrent valid initialization attempts produce exactly one successful publication; later attempts cannot replace it.
Current and all getters remain consistent after caller input mutation; InstanceId is stable during a run and differs between independently initialized application processes.
No production Reset API, mutable global operation context, global exception subscription, or output lifecycle side effect is introduced.

stories.user_story: As a core consumer, I want one immutable startup snapshot so that every component observes the same validated environment and identity.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Capture supported structured values within fixed bounds
stories.outcome: Event and scope attributes are portable owned values that cannot change after capture or trigger unrestricted serialization.

tasks.description: Implement null, boolean, string, finite floating-point, safe-range integer, explicit large-integer string, invariant decimal-string, array, and string-keyed map representations.
Normalize supported UUID/time scalars to the contract representation; reject arbitrary objects without reflection serialization or arbitrary ToString calls.
Recursively copy input maps and arrays while enforcing depth 8, 1024 total attribute nodes, key/control rules, and shared Unicode-scalar validation helpers.
Add language-neutral positive/negative fixtures for numeric boundaries, nonfinite numbers, decimals, nested mutation, oversized structures, and Unicode/control input.

acceptance_criteria.description: Integer-number input outside inclusive -9007199254740991 through 9007199254740991 is rejected; explicit integer strings and decimal strings preserve their documented type.
Mutating any original nested collection after capture cannot alter owned values; unsupported or cyclic/excessively nested input terminates with a bounded rejection.
The attribute root counts as depth 1 and one node, and boundary fixtures distinguish exactly-at-limit from over-limit input.
No input automatically changes JSON type as its magnitude grows, and rejected input is available to the caller as a stable capture error for InvalidEvent accounting.

stories.user_story: As an event producer, I want supported structured values to be copied and bounded so that later caller mutations cannot alter recorded facts.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Project exceptions into bounded immutable event data
stories.outcome: Logs retain useful exception detail without keeping mutable exception graphs or permitting an unbounded event envelope.

tasks.description: Project exception type, message, optional stack trace, and inner exceptions into the section 9 shape at capture time.
Preserve AggregateException child order and enforce 16 nodes, inner depth 4, 4096 scalar values per exception message, and 16384 per stack trace.
Mark projections with truncated=true only where exception content was clipped; never retain Exception.Data or arbitrary exception properties.
Add deterministic fixtures for single/aggregate/nested exceptions, all limits, Unicode clipping, and exclusion of mutable data.

acceptance_criteria.description: Single inner exceptions use an array of one; aggregate children retain their original order and the required type/message fields.
Every exception-specific limit is enforced during traversal, with a truncation marker where required rather than malformed or incomplete JSON.
Changing Exception.Data after capture has no effect, and projected records contain no automatic HTTP body/header or environment-variable capture.
The result is an owned immutable projection with no retained mutable exception graph; its truncation and size information is available to the later aggregate event capture check in WP04-S04.

stories.user_story: As an operator, I want useful bounded exception detail so that a failure is understandable without retaining arbitrary mutable exception data.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Implement operation scopes across asynchronous work
stories.outcome: Concurrent operations retain their own operation IDs and attributes without altering shared environment identity.

tasks.description: Implement runtime-specific asynchronous scope storage and BeginScope using copied OperationContextData and the supported value model.
Apply outer-to-inner precedence, enforce maximum scope depth 32, and expose a captured merged scope view for event creation.
Implement LIFO disposal in the owning logical flow, harmless repeated disposal, and an out-of-order error that leaves scope state unchanged.
Add barrier-driven tests for nested scopes, child-task inheritance, two concurrent operations, independent runtimes, cancellation, input mutation, and invalid disposal order.

acceptance_criteria.description: Concurrent asynchronous operations do not exchange operation IDs or attributes; separate runtime instances keep separate scope chains.
Inner values override outer values, scope input is immutable after BeginScope, and the 33rd nested scope is rejected as specified.
Out-of-order disposal throws InvalidOperationException without changing the active scope; repeated correct-flow disposal is harmless.
Documentation states normal execution-context inheritance and prohibits passing scope handles to another concurrent flow for disposal.

stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want operation context to follow asynchronous work so that concurrent jobs keep distinct identifiers and attributes.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Create complete immutable events with metadata and W3C correlation
stories.outcome: Every captured event carries the correct producer identity, operation facts, bounded exception data, and correlation that existed at the logging call.

tasks.description: Implement the allowlisted event/resource projection from EnvironmentSnapshot, scope context, method severity, and LogEventData; keep configuration and destinations out of event metadata.
Apply explicit-event-over-scope attribute and OperationId precedence, trim optional identifiers, and reserve identity and trace/span fields against free-form overrides.
Capture valid W3C Activity.Current IDs and UTC time before admission; omit both IDs for absent/invalid/non-W3C activity and preserve the separate operation ID.
Implement the shared bounded contract encoder/size validation, including UTF-8 escaping, exact timestamp representation, field length/control rules, and the 64 KiB JSONL cap including LF.
Add structural fixtures for every field/null/severity mapping, delayed consumption after scope/activity changes, child activities, concurrent operations, and aggregate-size rejection.

acceptance_criteria.description: All required identity fields and every available allowlisted resource field appear; optional unavailable values are omitted and explicit attribute null remains JSON null.
Captured trace IDs have 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters and span IDs have 16, neither all zero; later Activity or scope changes cannot change queued evidence.
Explicit attributes and nonblank event OperationId win the documented scope precedence, while reserved identity/correlation stays unchanged.
Timestamp and numeric/string types match the shared schema; record size is checked after escaping, and an oversized event is rejected globally before any output admission.
Messages/templates retain supplied text within their limits, ordinary oversized input is rejected, and only the documented exception projection may clip content.

stories.user_story: As an event consumer, I want complete immutable event records so that identity, context, and trace correlation describe the actual logging call.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Implement logger filtering, deferred capture, and write outcomes
stories.outcome: Callers use one small logging API with predictable early exits, one event capture, and truthful per-output admission results.

tasks.description: Implement runtime-bound CreateLogger, IsEnabled, Write, and WriteLazy against an internal output-admission seam; use method severity as the sole level authority.
Implement the exact argument-validation, Stopped, Filtered, all-interested-faulted Rejected, capture, and admission decision order.

Evaluate an interested lazy factory at most once, return global InvalidEvent for capture rejection, and map per-output outcomes into Accepted/PartiallyAccepted/Rejected without inventing sequence numbers.
Add outcome-table tests with controllable output-interest/admission doubles, including None after stop, disabled outputs, differing thresholds, faults, queue-full results, and throwing factories.

acceptance_criteria.description: Stopped, Filtered, and all-faulted early rejection do not traverse content or invoke the factory; a valid None call after admission closes returns Stopped.
A file interested in Debug causes one lazy evaluation even when console is Warning; full queues never trigger a second factory invocation.
Accepted/PartiallyAccepted/Rejected and output statuses match actual admission attempts; only successful admissions receive sequence numbers and InvalidEvent has no output admission entries.
IsEnabled is not represented as a capacity reservation; caller factory exceptions retain their own failure, and normal output I/O failures cannot escape through logging calls.

stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want predictable filtering and write outcomes so that expensive diagnostics are deferred and admission results are truthful.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

Implement normal and verbose human renderers with the specified fields, available context, exception detail, and control-sequence escaping.
Keep rendering separate from threshold and destination selection; do not infer format from terminal/debugger state or add a message-template parser.
Add structural JSON fixtures and human-information assertions covering Unicode, newlines, exceptions, empty optional fields, and independent presentation settings.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each JSONL line independently parses and preserves required identity, severity, field types, optional omission, and metadata without banners, ANSI, raw multiline text, or a BOM.
Verbose human output includes available application/build/environment, operation, attributes, and exception detail; normal output includes timestamp, severity, component, event name, and message.
Changing detail or format never changes filtering or captured facts; untrusted text cannot inject terminal control commands or fake record boundaries.
Comparers normalize only documented nondeterministic fields and do not treat JSON property order or human spacing as an accidental permanent contract.

stories.user_story: As a person or machine consuming logs, I want selectable human and JSONL representations of the same event so that presentation changes preserve its meaning.
stories.business_case_role: Planned behavior and verification coverage; passing evidence is recorded during implementation.

stories.title: Admit events through independent bounded output queues
stories.outcome: Producer calls remain independent of slow output I/O, with bounded storage and an explicit outcome for each interested destination.

tasks.description: Create one bounded Channel and sequential worker per enabled output, using Wait full mode with nonblocking TryWrite, SingleReader=true, SingleWriter=false, and AllowSynchronousContinuations=false.

Reject incoming events at a full output, preserve previously admitted work, and produce independent output results without promising a total order across destinations.
Add barrier-driven multi-producer, saturation, blocked-writer, and output-threshold tests using controllable writers and bounded worker bookkeeping.

acceptance_criteria.description: A saturated output returns QueueFull for the incoming event and never evicts an older accepted event; accepted tickets exist only for successful admission.
A blocked file output does not block console admission or reorder console delivery; accepted records retain each output's admission order.
Queue capacity and outstanding worker bookkeeping remain within the documented bounds under bursts and concurrent producers.
Mixed destination outcomes produce the correct partial-acceptance result, and no enqueue result is described as a delivery or durability acknowledgment.

stories.user_story: As an application developer, I want independent bounded output admission so that slow I/O cannot block producer calls or silently evict accepted work.

tasks.description: Maintain cumulative per-output filtered/attempted/accepted/rejected/written/failed/abandoned counters, nonnegative pending/in-flight gauges, and the runtime-wide InvalidEvent count.
Update delivery only after complete success is confirmed, capture consistent observation boundaries, and retain partial/uncertain writes as failed or pending according to their actual terminal state.
Implement Running/Faulted/Stopping/Stopped output transitions; terminal I/O failure closes admission, records the in-flight outcome, abandons unattempted queued work, and retains fault information.
Expose immutable GetDiagnostics snapshots separately from normal routing, without recursive retries; add fault/partial-write/blocked-write and counter-invariant tests with controllable writers.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every consistently captured boundary satisfies Accepted = Written + Failed + Abandoned + Pending; dequeuing alone never increments Written.
InvalidEvent increments the global counter without an output admission or sequence; pending gauges can decrease while cumulative counters never reset or decrease.
One terminally failed output rejects new work and abandons unattempted accepted events while other outputs continue; v1 does not automatically retry a possibly partial write.
Diagnostics remain available after fault/stop, preserve the last fault, and cannot create a recursive log loop, unbounded retry queue, or unbounded diagnostic tasks.

stories.user_story: As an operator, I want truthful delivery accounting and output fault isolation so that loss and unresolved work remain visible.

Wire file and console outputs into runtime startup so any enabled-file initialization failure stops newly created workers and releases handles/ownership without deleting pre-existing segments.

tasks.description: Atomically close admission and capture stop boundaries on the first StopAsync call, start one operation with the configured monotonic overall deadline, and make later calls join it.

Coordinate final handle/ownership release with eventual I/O completion, preserve immutable results and later diagnostics, and avoid disposal beneath unresolved writes or replacement-write loops.

DisposeAsync is idempotent and joins the same operation; unsuccessful drain remains visible through stop results/diagnostics, with no second drain window or deletion of pre-existing log evidence.
Returned observations remain immutable if a blocked write later completes; ownership is released only through the documented safe coordination, and tests make no exactly-once/crash-durable promise.
